acceptance.given: A historical target is subjected to rename or delete through the governed write path.

oracle.expected: Both rename and delete attempts are rejected and the historical target bytes and identity remain unchanged.
oracle.observable: The guarded write operation returns rejection for each attempt and a before/after snapshot comparison shows identical historical target state.

acceptance.then: The immutability decision is evaluated after each attempted write.
acceptance.when: Execute isolated rename and delete attempts against a historical target while all non-target inputs remain constant.

failure_intents.selector_intent: A fixture where the governed write path allows rename or delete of a historical target must fail because historical state changes.
A verification run without a complete before/after historical-state snapshot must fail closed as unverifiable.

affected_subjects: Historical state immutability for rename/delete writes
slice_hint.behavior_change: Reject rename and delete writes targeting historical state while preserving historical bytes and identity.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No schema change; rollback restores prior guard behavior without mutating historical data.

slice_hint.state_transition: historical target remains immutable after rejected rename/delete attempts
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Both attempted operations are rejected and historical state before equals historical state after.

acceptance.given: The NFR-5 verification fixture is prepared for rename and delete attempts.

oracle.expected: Recorded verification demonstrates that only the rename/delete operation varies and all other inputs are constant.
forbidden: A fixture that does not isolate the target mutation
oracle.observable: Verification evidence contains a fixture comparison proving sole variation of the rename/delete attempt.

acceptance.then: Isolation is checked before interpreting the rejection result.
acceptance.when: Run the isolated rename/delete-attempt verification fixture and inspect its controlled-input evidence.

failure_intents.selector_intent: A fixture that changes any non-target input alongside rename/delete must fail the verification guard for lack of isolation.
Verification evidence missing the controlled-input comparison must fail artifact validation.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Add an explicit harness guard and fixture comparison proving rename/delete is the sole changed input in immutability verification.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No schema change; remove isolation guard while retaining historical-state protection on rollback.

slice_hint.state_transition: verification remains pending until controlled-input comparison passes
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Fixture comparison proves only rename/delete varies, then records the rejection verification.

acceptance.given: The FR-9 Acceptance consumer evaluates an otherwise valid closure input with the caller field omitted.

oracle.expected: The Acceptance consumer rejects closure solely because caller is omitted.
forbidden: Any non-caller input changed in the omission fixture
oracle.observable: Acceptance evaluation returns a closure-reject result with an omitted-caller reason.

acceptance.then: The caller-presence rule is evaluated before closure acceptance.
acceptance.when: Evaluate the isolated FR-9 omission fixture through the Acceptance consumer.

failure_intents.selector_intent: An Acceptance consumer that accepts closure when caller is omitted must fail the omission fixture.
An omission fixture that changes fields other than caller must fail the isolation guard.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Require a non-omitted caller for Acceptance-consumer closure and return a deterministic closure-reject reason when absent.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No schema change; rollback restores prior closure policy.

slice_hint.state_transition: valid closure candidate with omitted caller transitions to closure reject
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Acceptance consumer returns reject and identifies omitted caller while all other fixture inputs remain unchanged.

acceptance.given: A candidate descriptor names itself as the validator while every other descriptor and evaluation input is unchanged.

oracle.expected: Trust is rejected with a self-selected-validator reason and no trusted Replay Result is produced.
forbidden: A trusted Replay Result is produced from candidate self-selection
oracle.observable: The isolated candidate-descriptor evaluation returns trust-rejected and emits no trusted Replay Result.

acceptance.then: The validator identity binding rule is evaluated before any trust result is emitted.
acceptance.when: Evaluate the candidate descriptor against the validator identity policy using the isolated self-selection fixture.

failure_intents.selector_intent: A validator policy that trusts a candidate-selected validator identity must fail the self-selection fixture.
An evaluation artifact containing a trusted Replay Result for candidate self-selection must fail result-integrity validation.

affected_subjects: Replay trust decision for validator identity binding
slice_hint.behavior_change: Reject trust when the candidate descriptor selects its own validator identity and suppress trusted Replay Result production.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No schema change; rollback restores prior evaluator behavior without altering stored evidence.

slice_hint.state_transition: candidate self-selection transitions evaluation to trust rejected
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Trust decision is rejected and no trusted Replay Result exists for the self-selection case.
